nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous LMAN1 variants on chromosome 18q21. Most are null alleles that abolish LMAN1 protein expression; the rare missense variants (W67S, C475R) produce unstable protein or defective mannose and MCFD2 binding.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment protein ERGIC-53 cause combined deficiency of coagulation factors V and VIII.
evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescence and Western analysis of immortalized lymphocytes from patients homozygous for either of the two mutations demonstrate complete lack of expression of the mutated gene in these cells.

evidence.reference_title: Combined deficiency of coagulation factors V and VIII: an update.
evidence.snippet: Only two missense mutations have been identified in LMAN1, including W67S and C475R.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous MCFD2 variants on chromosome 2p21, including null alleles, a large 5' regulatory deletion, and missense or C-terminal truncating variants that disrupt the calcium-dependent EF-hand fold MCFD2 needs to bind LMAN1.

evidence.reference_title: Bleeding due to disruption of a cargo-specific ER-to-Golgi transport complex.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that inactivating mutations in MCFD2 cause F5F8D with a phenotype indistinguishable from that caused by mutations in LMAN1.

evidence.reference_title: Deletion of 3 residues from the C-terminus of MCFD2 affects binding to ERGIC-53 and causes combined factor V and factor VIII deficiency.
evidence.snippet: a large deletion of 8.4 kb eliminating the 5'UTR of the gene and a nonsense mutation resulting in the deletion of only 3 amino acids (DeltaSLQ) from the C-terminus of MCFD2

nodes.description: The only available source of factor V, since no factor V concentrate exists. Used for bleeding episodes and to cover surgery, typically targeting factor V activity of about 15%. nodes.description: The LMAN1-MCFD2 receptor also exports alpha-1-antitrypsin. Knockout mice and knockout hepatoma cells accumulate it in the hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum and secrete less of it. No liver or lung consequence has been reported in patients, so this node has no clinical downstream.

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of MCFD2- and LMAN1-deficient mice demonstrates distinct functions in vivo.
evidence.snippet: Comparable accumulation of AAT was observed in hepatocyte ER of singly and doubly deficient mice, demonstrating a role for LMAN1 and MCFD2 in efficient ER exit of AAT.

evidence.reference_title: LMAN1-MCFD2 complex is a cargo receptor for the ER-Golgi transport of α1-antitrypsin.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report that LMAN1 and MCFD2 knockout (KO) HepG2 and HEK293T cells display reduced AAT secretion and elevated intracellular AAT levels due to a delayed ER-to-Golgi transport of AAT.

nodes.description: Without the cargo receptor, newly made factor V (in hepatocytes) and factor VIII (in endothelial cells) leave the endoplasmic reticulum inefficiently, so less of each is secreted. Export is reduced rather than abolished, which is why plasma levels fall to roughly 5-30% of normal rather than to zero.

nodes.description: LMAN1 and MCFD2 form a calcium-dependent cargo receptor that cycles between the endoplasmic reticulum and the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment. The LMAN1 carbohydrate recognition domain holds separable binding sites for MCFD2 and for high-mannose glycans on factor V and factor VIII, and the MCFD2 EF-hand domains bind both LMAN1 and the cargo. Loss of either subunit, or any missense variant that prevents the two from associating, removes a functional receptor.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular basis of LMAN1 in coordinating LMAN1-MCFD2 cargo receptor formation and ER-to-Golgi transport of FV/FVIII.
evidence.snippet: Thus, the CRD of LMAN1 contains distinct, separable binding sites for both its partner protein (MCFD2) and the cargo proteins (FV/FVIII).

evidence.reference_title: EF-hand domains of MCFD2 mediate interactions with both LMAN1 and coagulation factor V or VIII.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that the EF-hand domains of MCFD2 contain separate binding sites for LMAN1 and FV/FVIII that are essential for cargo receptor formation and cargo loading in the ER.

evidence.snippet: The interaction is independent of sugar-binding of ERGIC-53 and involves most of the missense mutation sites of MCFD2 so far reported in F5F8D.

evidence.snippet: However, the safety of off-label use of FVIIa in treating F5F8D remains to be established.

nodes.description: Plasma factor V and factor VIII activities fall together, usually to 5-30% of normal (typically 10-20%). Mean levels are lower in MCFD2-related than in LMAN1-related disease. Bleeding severity correlates poorly with factor levels, and two simultaneous deficiencies do not bleed more than a single factor V or factor VIII deficiency of similar degree.

evidence.reference_title: Combined deficiency of coagulation factors V and VIII: an update.
evidence.snippet: Diagnosis is made on laboratory findings of decreased FV and FVIII levels in plasma, usually in the range of 5 to 30% of normal (typically 10–20%). No correlations of bleeding severity and the levels of FV and FVIII have been observed in F5F8D patients.

evidence.reference_title: Combined deficiency of coagulation factors V and VIII: an update.
evidence.snippet: Recent reports also confirmed the previous observation that defects of two factors do not lead to more severe bleeding symptoms than single defect of FV or FVIII of similar degree.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlation in combined deficiency of factor V and factor VIII.
evidence.snippet: Although there is considerable overlap, the mean levels of plasma FV and FVIII in patients with MCFD2 mutations are significantly lower than the corresponding levels in patients with LMAN1 mutations.

nodes.description: About a fifth of circulating factor V is stored in platelet alpha-granules and is derived from plasma factor V by megakaryocyte endocytosis. In this disorder the platelet pool is reduced to the same degree as plasma factor V.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-phenotype correlation in combined deficiency of factor V and factor VIII.
evidence.snippet: Measurement of platelet factor V (FV) levels in 7 F5F8D patients (4 with LMAN1 and 3 with MCFD2 mutations) demonstrated similar reductions to those observed for plasma FV.
